subject: Surveying and fitting around business operations
hook: Phased fitting keeps the office open while the furniture changes
ig:
Phased fitting keeps the office open while the furniture changes.

Here's the principle, laid out as a typical example. Instead of clearing the whole floor, the space is split into zones: perhaps reception, the desk area and the staff kitchen.

You decide which zone can be out of action first. All the furniture is made and checked in our workshop before work on site begins, so each zone's fit is short and predictable.

We fit one zone, check it, clean down and hand it back. Then we move to the next. Your staff shift around a little, but the business keeps running.

It takes more planning at survey, which is exactly where it belongs.

Swipe through the six stages, and send this to whoever manages your premises.
fb:
For businesses that can't close for a fit-out, a phased install is often the answer.

The principle is simple: split the space into zones, decide the order, build everything in the workshop first, then fit, check and hand back one zone at a time. Customer-facing areas can be done out of hours, and nobody has to work in a building site for long.

The carousel shows a typical example from survey to sign-off. Planning something similar? Here's more on our commercial cabinet making:

on_asset: F1: Survey and zone — The space is split into zones, for example reception, open-plan desks and the staff kitchen, each with its own fit window. | F2: Agree the order — The business picks which zone can be out of use first. Customer-facing areas often go out of hours. | F3: Workshop build — Every zone's furniture is made and checked in our Hanley workshop before any on-site work starts. | F4: Zone one fitted — Furniture is positioned, levelled and fixed. Noisy fixing is booked around calls and appointments. | F5: Check and hand back — Each zone is checked, cleaned down and handed back before the next is started. | F6: Final walk-round — Doors and drawers adjusted, the contact signs off, and the team moves in fully.
